text:
maya: Quick follow-up from the quantization RFC — we need to decide on a precision-budget abstraction and how the runtime surfaces fallbacks for FP8/INT8/4bit. TL;DR: propose a small refactor of the runtime policy API and a conservative rollout plan.

owen: +1. can you sketch the API change?

maya: idea: expose a `precision_budget` object per model-route that contains: target_quality (p99 of eval score), max_cost_ratio, fallback_chain (ordered list), and telemetry_tags. runtime picks highest precision satisfying budget.

sasha: example config would help. also how do we compute "quality" at runtime? offline eval only or online signals?

maya: example config:```json
{
  "precision_budget": {
    "target_quality": "0.98_bleu_agg",
    "max_cost_ratio": 1.15,
    "fallback_chain": ["fp8","int8","4bit"],
    "telemetry_tags": ["qa_set:v2","route:chat"]
  }
}
```

lia: For quality we should gate on offline evals (prompt sets) + sampling-based online drift checks. runtime does not measure BLEU live; it uses a short-circuit signal from quality monitor to increment a `quality_penalty` and force higher precision for affected keys.

bryan: how to enforce cost_ratio? will runtime estimate token cost per precision and compute expected cost for request?

maya: yes — runtime has per-model per-precision unit-cost estimates (tokens/sec and $/token). `max_cost_ratio` is relative to baseline (e.g., fp8 baseline = 1.0). if expected cost exceeds budget, choose lower precision only if quality budget permits.

owen: edge case: long-form requests where cost estimate is high mid-request because of continuation. do we re-evaluate mid-stream?

sasha: we can allow mid-request hot-swap only if KV cache formats compatible. otherwise we must fallback between requests. hot-swap complexity is high. suggest: no mid-request precision changes for now. mark as future work.

lia: operational concerns: telemetry needs tags for precision, fallback_reason, eval_snapshot_id, and a short hash of prompt family. this avoids sending PII.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created ephemeral canary cluster `quant-budget-canary-03` with fp8/int8/4bit variants. logs forwarded to /infra/quant-canary.

bryan: rollout plan I propose: 1) API & config proto change 2) offline evaluator integration (compute target_quality per route) 3) canary on small traffic 4) metric-based rollback if quality delta > threshold.

maya: rollback thresholds: if user-visible eval score drop > 1.5% absolute or if error-rate spike > 0.5% over baseline -> rollback. also cost anomalies (spend > 30% predicted) -> alert.

owen: testing: we need a synthetic prompt family generator that stresses low-bit quantization failure modes (numeric stability, repetition collapse). add to perf-evals.

sasha: also add a fuzz harness for per-layer quant traces so we can detect which layers amplify error. that will inform fallback granularity later (per-layer vs per-model).

lia: interface boundary question: should `precision_budget` live in model catalog metadata or per-route? I think per-route (customer can override) but catalog provides defaults and suggested profiles.

maya: agreed. catalog defaults + route override. catalog entry should include the `quality_curve` mapping precision->expected_eval_score and cost estimates. runtime uses that as prior.

bryan: ownership: eng-ml owners `maya` and `sasha` to implement policy + eval hooks. eng-runtime `owen` to add selection logic and cost estimator. infra to run canaries. devex to update config docs.

maya: deliverables and rough timeline: week1: proto + catalog schema, week2: evaluator + telemetry tags, week3: runtime selection + canary, week4: monitor + rollout playbook.

owen: minor nit: make `fallback_chain` accept conditional entries like {"int8":"only_for_short_prompts"} so we can encode constraints. keep initial version simple (list of strings) and add conditional entries as v2.

sasha: agree. add lint that validates `precision_budget` does not contradict model capabilities (e.g., some models don't support fp8).

lia: testing checklist: offline evals, canary with 1% traffic, synthetic stress, rollback automation test, telemetry downstream consumer validation.

bryan: can we push a small demo route for product so they can try different budgets? team OK with a `quant-sandbox` route?

maya: yes, `quant-sandbox` created. limited quota and only internal tokens. infra-bot already provisioned it. :party_parrot:

owen: I'll start a PR to add `precision_budget` proto and open a follow-up RFC for hot-swap later.

sasha: ping me on the PR for the eval curve format.

maya: thanks all. I'll write the rollout playbook and post it here tomorrow.

lia: ack.

bryan: thanks — feel good about this plan.

maya: action items: maya (playbook + catalog defaults), owen (runtime selector + cost estimator), sasha (eval curves + layer fuzz), lia (telemetry + tests), bryan (rollout/checklist).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster `quant-budget-canary-03` is live and receiving 0.8% of traffic.
